children: The company separately secures an order for two utility-scale BESS projects in South Africa, with a combined storage capacity of 616 MWh

Shares of Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy rose sharply in early trade on Tuesday after the renewable energy engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company announced orders worth more than Rs 985 crore, including a 534.3 MWp solar project in Rajasthan and two battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in South Africa.
The stock climbed as much as 7.44 per cent to Rs 186.25 on the BSE. At 9.27 a.m., it was trading 5.45 per cent higher at Rs 182.80, while the BSE Sensex was largely unchanged at around 74,875.
The order wins span both solar and energy storage, giving the company fresh business across its key renewable energy markets.

In India, Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy has secured a 534.3 MWp order from a leading independent power producer for a solar project in Rajasthan. The company will execute the Balance of System (BOS) package for the project. The order also marks the company’s engagement with a new customer.

The company has separately secured an order for two utility-scale BESS projects in South Africa, with a combined storage capacity of 616 MWh. The projects have been awarded by a Middle East-based renewable energy developer and will be executed as a turnkey EPC package.
The South African order comes from a repeat customer and is the company’s second-largest utility-scale BESS project to date, Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy said.
Together, the two orders are worth more than Rs 985 crore, including taxes.
The Rajasthan solar project is expected to reduce carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 0.80 million tonnes once commissioned.

“The two order wins reinforce our business momentum and reflect the confidence customers continue to place in our execution capabilities,” said Chandra Kishore Thakur, Global CEO, Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy.
Thakur said the orders also demonstrate the company’s customer relationships, project execution capabilities and access to a skilled workforce.
Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy is an end-to-end renewable energy EPC company with operations across utility-scale solar, floating solar, hybrid and energy storage, and wind projects.
The company has a portfolio exceeding 28.7 GWp across commissioned projects and projects under construction. Its solar operations and maintenance portfolio stands at 18.3 GWp.
The company operates across 28 countries, with a presence in India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, Australia and the Americas.
